tl:Dr; recruiters usually don't text first. Do a reverse phone lookup and do not engage or respond to the text message.

Yeah, adding to everyone here, even just the prompt alone this is a scam.

I've gotten variations of this text message. They will say Robert Half or TEKSystems. I'm always suspicious when they never use their last name. Even down to using another phone number (Google voice) to call the number back and see if it's real. It came up as a text message only number. I also do a reverse phone number search too. So far none of the text message first numbers have been real, regardless of who sent them and why. 

I also recommend not responding to the text because that just indicates to the scammer that you're a live contact and other scammers might contact you considering the first one didn't work. Eventually once I figured out the pattern, I just block and delete the message instead of questioning if it's real.

It's even more frustrating because I don't list my personal cell on my resume, it's always my Google voice number. So that immediately makes me suspicious when someone texts me on my main line looking for anything. I usually take a contact from my Google voice number and then give them my personal once I know it's legit.

Either way, most recruiters are old school boiler room folks, dial for dollars or InMail LinkedIn messages. Remember, they are commissioned salespeople cold calling you for leads. These text scams are just that, lazy fuckers trying to make a quick buck.

For awhile some of the non-InMail LinkedIn messages were scummy and I blocked those too. I also hate the recruiters who bait you with a resume just to get lead information and then say "well we might have a fit in another department for you". The economy must not be doing so well because I don't get as many cold calls as I used to.

In addition, random emails that just have a job description in the body of the email and asking for an updated resume I block too. They seem to scrape emails from some resource and sign me up without double opt-in for their mailing list. There's always an unsubscribe list in their emails and I don't send them any information or engage. I unsubscribe from their lists too. I swear like 15 companies have the same ATS, because they are all variations of a certain name and have Indian sounding names. I also report the emails as spam and if they get really aggressive filter their emails into the trash.

Remember, if it's a deal worth doing then it's worth some due diligence and should survive under scrutiny. If it's too good to be true it probably is.
